summary:
Implemented persistent traffic mirroring on node1 (Debian/SONiC-VS) using iptables mangle TEE targets: all traffic to/from node2 (10.100.28.11) is cloned in PREROUTING (incoming from node2) and OUTPUT (outgoing to node2) with gateway 10.100.28.12 (node3), preserving original src/dst addressing so node3's tcpdump sees packets "addressed elsewhere" while the original node1<->node2 path is untouched (0% packet loss throughout all tests). Config was made boot-persistent via a systemd oneshot unit (traffic-mirror.service, enabled) plus /etc/modules-load.d for xt_TEE. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot_id, mirroring state, working ping) on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified mirroring functionality end-to-end after each restart and once more after all three had cycled.

Note: an initial attempt using tc/mirred + gretap (ERSPAN-style) encapsulation was tried first but the mirrored frames never actually left node1's eth0 (kernel accepted them into the gretap device but they didn't reach node3), even though a manually-addressed GRE tunnel between the same endpoints worked fine — this was abandoned in favor of the iptables TEE approach, which worked immediately and is simpler/more standard for this passive-mirroring use case.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (Debian 13, SONiC-VS image) and node2/node3 (AlmaLinux 9) all share eth0 on 10.100.28.0/24, a switched (non-hub) segment
Confirmed baseline: node1<->node2 ping worked; node3 tcpdump on eth0 saw nothing of that traffic (proving real L2 switching, not a hub)

Attempted tc clsact + act_mirred + gretap ERSPAN-style mirroring on node1; verified gretap tunnel worked standalone via direct IP test but mirrored frames from tc never appeared on the wire — abandoned this approach
Cleaned up all tc filters/qdiscs and gretap interfaces on node1 and node3
Implemented iptables mangle TEE mirroring on node1: PREROUTING rule for traffic from node2, OUTPUT rule for traffic to node2, both with --gateway node3
Verified mirroring end-to-end: node3 tcpdump on eth0 captured node1<->node2 ICMP traffic (addressed to 10.100.28.10/.11), while original ping between node1 and node2 had 0% packet loss
Persisted mirroring config via /etc/modules-load.d/traffic-mirror.conf (xt_TEE) and a new systemd unit traffic-mirror.service (enabled, RemainAfterExit)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, machine-id, uptime, mirror service state) on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via systemd reboot (background-scheduled so ack returned first), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed TEE rules and service auto-restored, re-verified mirroring functionally
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, re-verified mirroring functionally with node1<->node2 traffic still flowing and node3 capturing it
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, ran final full end-to-end verification of mirroring across all three freshly-rebooted nodes

evidence.requirement: Baseline: node1<->node2 traffic flows normally and node3 does NOT see it before mirroring is configured
evidence.summary: Ping from node1 to node2 succeeded (0% loss) while a concurrent tcpdump on node3's eth0 captured zero packets, confirming the segment is a switched L2 domain requiring explicit mirroring.

evidence.requirement: Mirroring implementation delivers a copy of node1<->node2 traffic to node3 with original addressing preserved
evidence.summary: iptables mangle TEE rules installed on node1 (PREROUTING for src=node2, OUTPUT for dst=node2, gateway=node3); after pinging node1->node2, node3's tcpdump on eth0 captured both the echo request and reply packets addressed to 10.100.28.10/10.100.28.11, and the TEE rule counters incremented (4 and 8 packets matching the 4 pings).

evidence.requirement: Original node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing unaffected by the mirroring
evidence.summary: Multiple ping tests between node1 and node2 (before, during, and after mirroring setup, and after each restart) consistently showed 0% packet loss and normal latency.

evidence.requirement: Mirroring configuration persists across a node1 reboot (restart-survivability)
evidence.summary: Created and enabled systemd unit traffic-mirror.service plus /etc/modules-load.d entry for xt_TEE; after node1's restart the service was active and the TEE rules were present again automatically (0/0 packet counters, freshly reset).

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured on every node before restart (boot identity + working state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, machine-id, and uptime on node1, node2, and node3, plus node1's active mirror service and TEE rule counters, prior to any restarts.

evidence.requirement: node1 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity proven, then service/functionality recovery verified
evidence.summary: node1 reboot acknowledged before disconnect (background-scheduled), subsequent execs failed with connection reset (mid-reboot), then boot_id changed from 8e8823ec... to 5af44431..., systemd service and TEE rules confirmed active, and a fresh ping+tcpdump round-trip proved mirroring works post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity proven, then connectivity/mirroring recovery verified
evidence.summary: node2 reboot acknowledged before disconnect, boot_id changed from c2ffc729... to 453a66a3..., eth0 addressing restored (10.100.28.11/24), and a post-restart ping+tcpdump test confirmed node1<->node2 traffic still mirrored to node3.

evidence.requirement: node3 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity proven, then capture capability/mirroring recovery verified
evidence.summary: node3 reboot acknowledged before disconnect, boot_id changed from a0d04bc6... to 1b38f7c8..., eth0 addressing restored (10.100.28.12/24), and a final full end-to-end test after all three nodes had cycled showed node1<->node2 ping succeeding at 0% loss with node3's tcpdump capturing the mirrored ICMP request/reply pairs.
